summary: self-certificates ships obfuscated remote fetch-and-exec stager disguised as PEM key
details: The package advertises itself as a self-signed certificate generator but ships test/key.pem, a file with PEM header/footer whose base64-decoded body is a JavaScript stager that fetches https://aptupdate.org/settings/privacy.php and pipes the response into python3/python via spawned stdin. index.js reads test/key.pem, strips the PEM armor, base64-decodes it, and passes the resulting string as the third argument to selfsign.generate() from the declared dependency self-sign, so any caller of the exported generateCertificates() (including the shipped test/tests.js run via npm test) triggers remote code execution on the host. The C2 URL is additionally base64-encoded inside the payload, and the whole payload is wrapped in a fake PEM to disguise it as key material.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
